title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization & Regression Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook defines Redwood's integrated approach for model onboarding and ongoing evaluation across the Eval Harness, prompt set curation, quantization profile selection, quality guardrails, and regression triage. The goal is to provide a single, repeatable process (and templates) that engineering, applied ML, and product teams can follow to bring models into production with measurable quality and cost trade-offs.

Scope

Applies to: any model (open or customer-supplied) that will be served via Redwood APIs or Dedicated/Private deployments. Covers stages: initial onboarding, baseline benchmarking, quantization candidate evaluation, production rollout, and regression detection + triage.

Owners and roles

- Document owner: Applied ML (Aisha Patel)
- Eval harness owner: Eval Platform (Liam Zhang)
- Model onboarding reviewer: Model Ops (Maya Fernandez)
- Product stakeholder: (assigned per project)
- Oncall triage: SRE / Applied ML rotation

Principles

- Single source of truth: every onboarding must produce an Eval Report (JSON + human summary) stored in the eval-harness artifact store.
- Measurable thresholds: quality and latency SLOs must be set before rollout.
- Conservative quantization: prefer profiles with explicit eval traces showing negligible quality regression for the target prompt set.
- Fast triage: regressions must be detected automatically and have an owner, priority, and rollback path.

High-level workflow (steps)

1. Intake and scoping
   - Complete the Model Intake form (link to template).
   - Define primary intents and target prompt sets (see "Prompt Set Curation" below).
   - Set initial SLOs: latency P95 target, cost target per 1k tokens, quality thresholds per eval metric.

2. Baseline evaluation (unquantized)
   - Run Eval Harness baseline_suite on the model with the curated prompt sets (see required test matrix).
   - Capture tokens/second, P99 tail latency, and primary quality metrics (e.g., exact match, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, factuality score, safety/regulatory metrics).
   - Store results in artifact store and link to PR.

3. Quantization candidates
   - Generate quantized variants per standard profiles (int8, GPTQ-4bit, mixed FP16/INT8).
   - Re-run the baseline_suite and compare delta to baseline (statistical tests + significance).
   - If regression <= defined threshold (default: <0.5% absolute on core metric and no safety regressions), mark profile as candidate for canary.

4. Canary rollout and monitoring
   - Deploy the model variant to a canary route with 1-5% traffic.
   - Enable quality monitoring and prompt-set based canary checks.
   - Monitor for 48-72 hours, or until sample size reaches N (default 3k requests), whichever is longer.
   - If autotriage flags a regression, follow the Regression Triage Playbook (below).

5. Gradual rollout (Ramped)
   - On objective canary success, expand to 25% for 24 hours, then 50%, then 100% as traffic and SLOs permit.
   - Document final decision in the Eval Report and tag model version in the model catalog.

Prompt Set Curation (rules & checklist)

Purpose: prompt sets represent realistic production traffic distributions and edge cases used for both offline evals and online canary checks.

Checklist:
- Identify 3-5 primary intents (e.g., summarization, Q&A, code generation).
- For each intent include:
  - 200-500 in-distribution prompts (representative production samples).
  - 100-200 out-of-distribution / adversarial prompts (edge cases and known failure modes).
  - 50-100 safety/sensitive prompts (toxicity, PII detection test cases).
- Label each prompt with metadata: intent, source (prod/seeded/generated), expected output type (classification/freeform/structured), and difficulty tier.
- Ensure a holdout set (20%) for validation used only in final verification runs.

Curation guidelines:
- Prefer real product logs (anonymized) for in-distribution sets.
- Seed edge cases from past incidents, community benchmarks, and SME input.
- Update prompt sets quarterly or after a major product change.

Benchmark matrix (example table)

Metric | Purpose | Threshold (example)
------ | ------- | ----------------
Accuracy / EM | intent correctness | >= 92% for core intents
Factuality score | hallucination control | >= 0.85 (aggregate)
Safety pass rate | toxicity/PPI detection | >= 99%
Latency P95 | user-perceived latency | <= 220 ms for hosted small-models
Cost per 1k tokens | economic guardrail | <= $0.80 (target; varies by model class)

Quantization profiles and evaluation matrix

We maintain canonical profiles with expected performance/quality tradeoffs. Always evaluate each profile against the full prompt set and safety checks.

Profile | Typical speedup | Acceptable use-cases
------- | -------------- | --------------------
FP16 (baseline) | 1x | Reference baseline for accuracy
INT8 (static) | 1.6-2x | Latency-sensitive services with minimal accuracy loss
GPTQ-4bit | 2-4x | Cost-sensitive batch workloads; require strict regression checks
Mixed FP16/INT8 | 1.8-2.5x | Balanced throughput + quality

Evaluation requirements per profile:
- Run full offline eval (all prompt sets + holdout).
- Compute per-intent deltas and per-prompt diff traces for debuggability.
- Run safety and PII detection regressions.
- Document artifacts and attach model card indicating recommended deployment modes.

Regression detection and triage playbook

Automated detection:
- Alerts are driven by two streams: offline eval regression deltas and production monitoring signals (quality checks sampled from production).
- Default alert thresholds:
  - Offline: decrease of core metric > 1.0% absolute OR safety regression > 0.5%
  - Online: rolling 1-hour drop in quality metric > 0.75% OR spike in error rate > 50% above baseline

Triage steps (ordered):
1. Triage owner acknowledges within 15 minutes.
2. Gather artifacts: Eval Report, recent canary logs, trace diffs, and example failing prompts.
3. Determine scope: isolated to prompt subsets, quantization variant, or upstream data change.
4. Immediate rollback decision: if safety regression confirmed or user-facing degradation > 2% absolute, rollback to previous stable model and notify stakeholders.
5. Hotfix or patch: prioritize and schedule a remediation run with clear owner and ETA.
6. Postmortem: create postmortem doc within 72 hours if impact > minor.

Runbook checklist for triage owner

- Verify alert provenance (offline vs online).
- Pull top 50 failing prompts and produce a short summary (3 bullets) of failure modes.
- If quantization suspected: re-run suspect requests against FP16 baseline and quantized model locally.
- If dataset drift suspected: run prompt distribution comparison tool (CLI: redwood-eval diff --baseline <baseline> --window 7d).
- Document decision and next steps in the incident thread.

Templates and examples

Eval Report JSON (minimal example):
{
  "model": "redwood-oss-xl-v1",
  "version": "2027-03-10",
  "profile": "gptq-4bit",
  "metrics": {
    "accuracy": "93.2",
    "factuality": "0.87",
    "safety_pass": "99.3"
  },
  "notes": "Candidate for canary after manual review. No safety regressions observed."
}

Onboarding checklist (short):
- [ ] Intake form completed
- [ ] Prompt sets uploaded and labeled
- [ ] Baseline eval complete and stored
- [ ] Quantization candidates evaluated
- [ ] Canary run planned and monitoring hooks configured
- [ ] Rollout decision recorded in Eval Report

Monitoring and tooling integration

- Eval Harness outputs artifacts to S3-compatible artifact store and registers run metadata in the Model Catalog.
- Canary monitors feed into Redwood Console: per-prompt metrics, cost dashboards, and anomaly detection.
- Autotriage service tags likely root causes using a rules engine and simple classifiers; manual review required for final decision.

Governance and cadence

- Quarterly review of prompt sets and quantization profiles by Applied ML and Product teams.
- Any model serving regulated or customer-sensitive PII must follow the Private Deployment onboarding checklist (link).

References

- Eval harness standards: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Prompt sets & benchmarks: /applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026
- Quantization profiles: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands

- Run local diff between models:
  redwood-eval run --baseline-model redwood-oss-xl-v1:fp16 --candidate-model redwood-oss-xl-v1:gptq-4bit --prompt-set prompts/core_intent.json --output artifacts/run-20270415.json
- Generate top failure report:
  redwood-eval analyze --artifact artifacts/run-20270415.json --top 50 --out analysis/top-50.csv

Last notes

This playbook is intended to be actionable for engineers and applied ML practitioners. If you have suggested changes or additions, please comment on this page or open a PR against the eval-harness repo with a link to the proposed update.
